source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 9.14 with Fig. 9.23 (PDF 213).

blocks.text: Ek circuit lein jis mein emf ε wali battery resistance R ke saath series mein jori hai (Fig. 9.23). Circuit mein steady (mustaqil) current I behta hai, aur resistor R ke terminals A aur B ke darmiyan steady potential difference V hai. Terminal A battery ke positive (+) pole se jura hai, is liye B se zyada potential par hai. Is circuit mein battery lagatar charge ko potential difference V ke "oopar" (uphill) uthati rehti hai. Potential difference ke matlab se, charge Q ko V ke oopar le jane mein kaam:
Yehi woh energy hai jo battery deti hai.
Battery jis rate se electrical energy deti hai, use battery ki power output ya electrical power kehte hain. Power ki definition (tareef) se:

blocks.text_alt: Electrical power = di gayi energy/laga waqt = V Q/t

blocks.alt: Mustateel circuit: baen taraf battery E, + oopar; daen taraf resistance R, terminal A (oopar) aur B (neeche); oopar ki taar par teer I daen taraf. Darmiyan dotted do-teer V oopar se neeche.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.23: battery ki power resistance R mein kharch hoti hai (kitab ki Figure 9.23 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: A battery ke + se jura hai is liye B se zyada potential par hai. Battery charge ko V ke barabar "oopar" uthati hai aur R mein woh energy heat (garmi) ban jati hai: P = VI.

Eq. 9.39 aam formula hai: voltage V par current I dene wala koi bhi source itni power deta hai. Fig. 9.23 ke circuit mein battery ki di hui power resistor R mein kharch (dissipate) hoti hai. Energy ki conservation (bachao) ke principle (usool) se resistor mein kharch hone wali power bhi Eq. 9.39 se milti hai:
Eq. 9.39 mein baari baari V = IR aur I = V/R rakhne se power ke aur formulas milte hain:

blocks.latex: P = V \times I = IR \times I = I^2R
blocks.text_alt: P = V × I = IR × I = I²R
P = V × I = V × V/R = V²/R

blocks.text: Is tarah resistor mein kharch hone wali power ke teen formulas hain:

blocks.latex: P = V \times I, \qquad P = I^2R, \qquad P = \frac{V^2}{R} \qquad (9.40)
blocks.text_alt: P = V × I,   P = I²R,   P = V²/R   (9.40)

blocks.text: V volts mein aur I amperes mein ho to power watts (W) mein aati hai.

blocks.caption: Power ke teen formulas: kab kaun sa

blocks.prompt: 500 W, 220 V bulb ke filament ki resistance 100 W, 220 V bulb se kam hai ya zyada (short question 9.7)? 50 m lamba aur 150 μm mota (diameter) copper ka taar 50 s tak 1 A current le jata hai; ρ = 1.69 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m le kar resistance aur paida hone wali heat nikalein (numerical 9.9).
blocks.explanation: R = V²/P: 500 W ke liye R = 220²/500 = 96.8 Ω; 100 W ke liye R = 48 400/100 = 484 Ω. Yani 500 W wale filament ki resistance kam hai. Taar ka area π(75 × 10⁻⁶ m)² = 1.77 × 10⁻⁸ m², is liye R = 1.69 × 10⁻⁸ × 50/1.77 × 10⁻⁸ = 47.8 Ω aur heat = I²Rt = 1² × 47.8 × 50 = 2.4 × 10³ J. Kitab ke jawab (4.8 GΩ aur 2.4 × 10¹¹ J) diye gaye data se nahi nikalte.

items: Battery charge Q ko V ke oopar uthati hai: W = VQ (9.38).
Power = energy per second (fi waqt) = VI (9.39); resistor mein P = VI = I²R = V²/R (9.40); unit watt.
